html:
Video Depth Anything (ByteDance): depth of a whole video, consistent from frame to frame, in windows of 32 frames on the Depth Anything V2 Small encoder; relative and metric. Apache-2.0 code and weights (Small only).

Commercial use: yes.

Details
  • Paper: Video Depth Anything: Consistent Depth Estimation for Super-Long Videos, CVPR 2025, 2025-01-21
  • Original code: https://github.com/DepthAnything/Video-Depth-Anything at 4f5ae23172ba
  • Code licence: Apache-2.0 (permissive); files: LICENSE
  • Weights licence: Apache-2.0
  • Licence evidence: https://github.com/DepthAnything/Video-Depth-Anything/blob/4f5ae23172ba60fd7bc11ef671cca678842c7072/LICENSE (Apache-2.0); https://huggingface.co/depth-anything/Video-Depth-Anything-Small/blob/256875362cff76724b920335dfb4b29dd611f66e/README.md (license: apache-2.0)
  • Training data: Depth Anything V2 Small encoder; the temporal head on synthetic video depth and pseudo-labelled real videos and images per the paper (arXiv 2501.12375)
  • Licence note: Only the Small checkpoints (relative and metric) are Apache-2.0; the Base and Large checkpoints are CC-BY-NC-4.0 and not included.
  • Licence note: The metric model is trained on Virtual KITTI 2 (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0) and IRS per the upstream README (a note only).
  • Options: short_side = 518 (>= 14; also input_size)
  • Kernel libraries: fastbb
  • Variants: video-depth-anything-s, video-depth-anything-metric-s
  • Outputs: inverse_depth, depth; kind: affine_invariant_inverse
  • Input size: any H x W >= 1, resized or padded inside the model
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): video-depth-anything-s 3000x4000 (1.8 GiB peak allocated, 3.5 reserved); video-depth-anything-metric-s 3000x4000 (1.8 GiB peak allocated, 3.5 reserved)
  • video-depth-anything-s 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 83 s (cold Inductor cache).
  • video-depth-anything-s original 1080x1920: upstream infer_video_depth(input_size=518, fp32=False): uint8 numpy frames in, numpy out (its API); the authors' autocast fp16
  • video-depth-anything-s portable 1080x1920, kernels 1080x1920: float CUDA frames in [0, 1] in, depth [L, H, W] on the device out
  • video-depth-anything-s load / first call: original 0.26 s / 14.043 s (1080x1920), portable 0.18 s / 1.455 s (1080x1920), kernels 0.12† s / 1.301 s (1080x1920)
  • † measured in the speed sweep after the portable load (or an earlier size) in the same process: file cache and kernels are warm, so the time is lower than a fresh start.
  • Protocol, one video per call (4 windows of 32 frames), first call, 1 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3; ms per video
  • Speed and memory not measured for: video-depth-anything-metric-s.

Measured

AbsRel / delta1 after a least-squares scale + shift fit (in disparity space for inverse-depth models), mean over images. Video: one call per sequence, one scale + shift per sequence, AbsRel / delta1 over all its pixels with Kinect depth, mean over sequences. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 1.3e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.42 % and p99 <= 0.55 % of the reference's median |value| (absolute error of the output inverse_depth).

Limitations

  • A call's batch is one video in time order: frames are not independent (each window attends over time and is aligned to the previous one), so a batch is not the same as single calls.
  • Every call runs at least one 32-frame window (shorter videos are padded with copies of their last frame): one image costs about as much as 32 frames in the temporal head.
  • The whole video's depth is kept on the device as float32 (L x H x W); split very long videos.
